findings.claim: For the quarter ended September 30, 2026, Brookfield reported consolidated net income of $1.914 billion versus $284 million a year earlier, net income attributable to shareholders of $1.305 billion versus $219 million, and distributable earnings of $1.718 billion, or $0.73 per share, up 16% per share from $0.63.
findings.source_title: Brookfield Corporation Reports 16% Increase in Earnings

findings.claim: Distributable earnings before realizations were a record $5.815 billion, or $2.47 per share, over the twelve months ended September 30, 2026, and fee-related earnings rose 15% from the prior-year quarter as fee-bearing capital increased 13% to $682 billion.
findings.source_title: Brookfield Corporation Reports 16% Increase in Earnings

findings.claim: Fundraising through the third quarter of 2026 totaled $123 billion, including $25 billion in the quarter, and after quarter-end Brookfield received $13 billion of additional commitments for its infrastructure flagship, taking capital committed to $26 billion, with a first close expected in the coming weeks.
findings.source_title: Brookfield Corporation Reports 16% Increase in Earnings

findings.claim: Wealth Solutions distributable earnings rose 22% from the prior-year quarter to $511 million, insurance assets were nearly $200 billion after the Just Group acquisition, and the P&C combined ratio was 99.6% in the quarter.
findings.source_title: Brookfield Corporation Reports 16% Increase in Earnings

findings.claim: Closing of the Just Group acquisition added $45 billion of insurance assets and took Wealth Solutions insurance assets to $191 billion as of June 30, 2026.

findings.claim: Brookfield ended the quarter with $207 billion of deployable capital, including $5.4 billion of liquidity at the Corporation, and said corporate debt had a 14-year weighted-average term with no remaining maturities in 2026; it also issued $600 million of five-year senior notes at 82 basis points over the benchmark.
findings.source_title: Brookfield Corporation Reports 16% Increase in Earnings

findings.claim: Brookfield repurchased over $300 million of Class A shares since the prior report and $889 million year to date, and the weighted-average share count for the quarter was 2,230.9 million versus 2,244.0 million a year earlier.
findings.source_title: Brookfield Corporation Reports 16% Increase in Earnings

findings.claim: At September 30, 2026, corporate borrowings were $16.056 billion, up from $14.301 billion at December 31, 2025, and non-recourse borrowings of managed entities were $266.013 billion, up from $245.311 billion.
findings.source_title: Brookfield Corporation Reports 16% Increase in Earnings

findings.claim: Interest expense on same-store non-recourse borrowings was $4.199 billion in the third quarter of 2026, and interest on corporate borrowings was $198 million.

findings.claim: Distributable earnings from Brookfield Property Group were $727 million over the twelve months ended September 30, 2026, down from $853 million in the prior twelve-month period, and the corporate-costs-and-other drag widened to $237 million in the quarter from $140 million a year earlier.

policy_links.policy: Framework agreement among Westinghouse, the U.S. federal government and Korea to accelerate nuclear development in the United States
policy_links.revenue_mechanism: Brookfield said the agreement strengthens the outlook for its Westinghouse energy business, but the release did not disclose a contract value or booked revenue.

key_risks.risk: Non-recourse borrowings of managed entities were $266.0 billion at September 30, 2026, and same-store interest on that debt was $4.2 billion in the quarter. The debt is largely non-recourse and corporate maturities are clear through 2026, but asset-level leverage can still reduce cash available to the parent if rates stay high or asset values fall.

The December 1, 2026 combination folds the investment parent together with a wealth and insurance platform that already holds nearly $200 billion of insurance assets and earned a 99.6% P&C combined ratio in the third quarter, so insurance results will sit closer to the public share.
Property-group distributable earnings fell over the last twelve months, and the Q2 report cited lower valuations on certain U.S. office properties in the value-add portfolio.

Options, escrowed shares and affiliate exchangeable shares added 116.0 million shares to the diluted count, about 5% of the 2,230.9 million weighted-average shares, even while the company was repurchasing stock.

notes: Brookfield is a Canadian foreign private issuer and reports under IFRS on Form 6-K and Form 40-F, not a 10-Q. The Q3 2026 figures are from the November 12, 2026 earnings release; the corresponding 6-K was not yet on EDGAR at the time of this write-up, and the release says the figures are unaudited. No equity offering, ATM or new convertible issuance was found in the last twelve months; the share count fell with buybacks, while 116 million existing options and exchangeable shares remain dilutive. Per-share figures in the release are adjusted for the three-for-two split completed on October 9, 2025, which is just outside the twelve-month window. The Westinghouse framework is described only in Brookfield's release, with no contract value, so evidence_of_company_revenue is false. Gross accumulated unrealized carried interest was $13.0 billion at quarter end; that balance is not included above as realized earnings.
